```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

violations <- tar_read(violations)
numeric_summary <- tar_read(numeric_summary_all)
level_summary <- tar_read(level_summary_all)
invariant_checks <- tar_read(invariant_check_all)
grain <- tar_read(grain_all)
manifest <- tar_read(data_manifest)
schema <- tar_read(dataschema)
exposures <- tar_read(exposure_registry)

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
id_order <- function(x) factor(x, levels = unique(x[order(as.numeric(x))]))
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 9))
```

A permanent QA tool, rebuilt whenever a dataset changes.
Nothing here is a pipeline failure: each finding is something to look at, and ends in a harmonisation fix, an analysis exception or no action.
Data: `r nrow(manifest)` datasets, overall hash `r unique(manifest$overall_hash)`.

## Findings by check

```{r}
#| label: findings-summary
check_labels <- c(
  above_max = "Numeric value above the schema maximum",
  below_min = "Numeric value below the schema minimum",
  outside_allowed_values = "Level not in the schema's allowed values (advisory)",
  screen_constant = "Screen-time variable with one distinct value in a wave",
  screen_all_zero = "Screen-time variable all zero in a wave",
  screen_nearly_all_zero = "Screen-time variable 99% or more zero in a wave (advisory)",
  screen_scale = "Screen-time variable far from other datasets (possible unit error)",
  usual_day_mismatch = "Usual-day value differs from its weekday and weekend rows",
  invariant_varies = "Row held constant takes more than one value within a participant",
  carry_gap = "Carried row has a value at some waves and none at others",
  carried_value_changes = "Carried row: different answers at different waves (advisory)",
  duplicate_key = "More than one row per participant, wave and measure",
  missing_participant_id = "Rows with no participant ID"
)
violations |>
  summarise(
    datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id),
    variables = n_distinct(variable_name, na.rm = TRUE),
    findings = n(),
    affected = sum(n),
    .by = c(check, severity)
  ) |>
  mutate(Check = coalesce(check_labels[check], check)) |>
  arrange(severity, desc(findings)) |>
  transmute(Check, Severity = severity, Datasets = datasets, Variables = variables, Findings = findings, `Cells or participants` = fmt(affected)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrr")
```

## Findings by dataset

```{r}
#| label: findings-by-dataset
violations |>
  filter(severity == "review") |>
  count(dataset_id, check) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = check, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(as.numeric(dataset_id)) |>
  rename(Dataset = dataset_id) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Findings to review, per dataset. Datasets with none are not listed.")
```

`r nrow(manifest) - n_distinct(violations$dataset_id[violations$severity == "review"])` of `r nrow(manifest)` datasets have no finding to review.
Ages over the schema's bound are advisory, because the preparation step's age rule removes those rows.

## Values outside the schema's bounds

The harmonisation guide keeps out-of-range scores for the analysis to screen, so these are expected in small numbers.
A large share in one dataset usually means a different score form or a mapping error.

```{r}
#| label: bounds
# Shares are of all of the dataset's values on the variable, in every wave
# and measure, and the extreme is the dataset's.
totals <- numeric_summary |>
  summarise(values = sum(n), lowest = min(min), highest = max(max), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name))
violations |>
  filter(check %in% c("above_max", "below_min")) |>
  summarise(cells = sum(n), waves = n(), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name, check, severity)) |>
  left_join(totals, by = c("dataset_id", "variable_name")) |>
  mutate(share = cells / values, extreme = ifelse(check == "above_max", highest, lowest)) |>
  arrange(severity, desc(share)) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, Check = check, Severity = severity, Cells = fmt(cells), `Share of the dataset's values` = pct(share), `Waves affected` = waves, `Most extreme value` = signif(extreme, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llllrrrr")
```

## Screen time

### Location and spread across datasets

Each line is one dataset's 5th to 95th percentile, with its quartiles and median, on the primary measure.
A dataset with several waves shows the average of its waves' percentiles, weighted by rows, which is close to but not the same as the percentile of all its rows.
Hours are bounded at 24, so a minutes-for-hours error shows mainly as values over the maximum; a dataset far from the others here is more likely a different question or population.

```{r}
#| label: screen-fn
hours_vars <- exposures$variable_name[exposures$unit %in% "hours"]
dataset_quantiles <- function(vars) {
  numeric_summary |>
    filter(variable_name %in% vars, st_measure_id == "primary") |>
    summarise(
      across(c(p05, p25, median, p75, p95), \(x) weighted.mean(x, n)),
      n = sum(n),
      .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name)
    )
}
quantile_plot <- function(vars, ncol = 3) {
  d <- dataset_quantiles(vars)
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  ggplot(d, aes(y = id_order(dataset_id))) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = p05, xmax = p95), colour = "grey60") +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = p25, xmax = p75), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(x = median), colour = "firebrick", size = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(vars(variable_name), scales = "free", ncol = ncol) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Dataset") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-screen-main
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 16
quantile_plot(c("st_total", "st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_comp", "st_tablet", "st_phone", "st_internet"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-screen-days
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 22
#| fig-cap: "Weekday and weekend rows of the same exposures."
quantile_plot(c(outer(c("st_total", "st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_comp"), c("_wd", "_we"), paste0)), ncol = 4)
```

```{r}
#| label: screen-high
numeric_summary |>
  filter(variable_name %in% hours_vars, st_measure_id == "primary") |>
  summarise(p95 = weighted.mean(p95, n), max = max(max), n = sum(n), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name)) |>
  filter(p95 >= 10) |>
  arrange(desc(p95)) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, N = fmt(n), `95th percentile (hours)` = signif(p95, 3), Maximum = signif(max, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "Dataset and variable pairs whose 95th percentile is 10 hours a day or more.")
```

### Scale, constant and usual-day findings

The usual-day check compares each row's usual-day value with (5 × weekday + 2 × weekend) / 7, on rows that have all three, as the harmonisation guide defines it.

```{r}
#| label: screen-findings
violations |>
  filter(check %in% c("screen_scale", "screen_constant", "screen_all_zero", "usual_day_mismatch")) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, Wave = wave, Measure = st_measure_id, Check = check, N = fmt(n), Detail = detail) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllllrl")
```

### Response bands and declared measure type

The number of distinct values a dataset records, against what `st_measure_type` says.
A "Continuous" measure with a handful of distinct values, or a banded one with many, deserves a look.

```{r}
#| label: measure-type
measure_type <- level_summary |>
  filter(variable_name == "st_measure_type", level != "Unknown") |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(dataset_id, st_measure_id)) |>
  select(dataset_id, st_measure_id, measure_type = level)
distinct_values <- numeric_summary |>
  filter(variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_total")) |>
  summarise(distinct = max(n_distinct), n = sum(n), .by = c(dataset_id, st_measure_id, variable_name)) |>
  left_join(measure_type, by = c("dataset_id", "st_measure_id"))
distinct_values |>
  mutate(band = cut(distinct, c(0, 4, 8, 15, 30, Inf), labels = c("1-4", "5-8", "9-15", "16-30", "31+"))) |>
  count(measure_type, band) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = band, values_from = n, values_fill = 0, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dataset, measure and variable combinations by declared type and number of distinct values.")
```

```{r}
#| label: measure-type-odd
distinct_values |>
  filter((measure_type == "Continuous" & distinct <= 8) | (measure_type == "Categorical" & distinct > 30)) |>
  arrange(measure_type, as.numeric(dataset_id), variable_name) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Measure = st_measure_id, Variable = variable_name, `Declared type` = measure_type, `Distinct values` = distinct, N = fmt(n)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llllrr", caption = "The combinations worth a look: declared continuous with 8 or fewer distinct values, or declared categorical with more than 30. Sums of banded items can rightly give many values.")
```

```{r}
#| label: near-zero
violations |>
  filter(check == "screen_nearly_all_zero") |>
  summarise(waves = n(), zero = sum(n), values = sum(denominator), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name)) |>
  arrange(as.numeric(dataset_id), variable_name) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, Waves = waves, `Share zero` = pct(zero / values), `Values above zero` = fmt(values - zero)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "Screen-time variables where 99% or more of a wave's values are zero.")
```

## Carried rows

The harmonisation guide treats these rows in three ways, recorded in `analysis/invariants.csv`.
A row held **constant** (sex, strata, cluster, trial arm) must take one value per participant.
A **carried** row keeps what was observed and fills waves where it was missing or not asked, so a participant may rightly hold two answers, but should not have a value at some waves and none at others.
An **onset** age is carried except to waves before onset, so neither test applies.

```{r}
#| label: invariants
rules <- tar_read(invariants)
invariant_checks |>
  left_join(rules[c("variable_name", "rule")], by = "variable_name") |>
  summarise(
    datasets = n(),
    repeated = sum(participants_repeated),
    varying = sum(participants_varying),
    gap = sum(participants_gap),
    .by = c(rule, variable_name)
  ) |>
  arrange(rule, variable_name) |>
  transmute(Rule = rule, Variable = variable_name, Datasets = datasets, `Participants seen twice or more` = fmt(repeated), `More than one value` = fmt(varying), `Value at some waves only` = fmt(gap)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: invariants-detail
violations |>
  filter(check %in% c("invariant_varies", "carry_gap")) |>
  mutate(share = n / pmax(denominator, 1)) |>
  arrange(check, desc(share)) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, Check = check, Participants = fmt(n), `Of those seen twice or more` = pct(share)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllrr", caption = "Findings to review on constant and carried rows.")
```

## Grain

```{r}
#| label: grain
grain |>
  summarise(rows = sum(rows), participants = sum(participants), duplicate_keys = sum(duplicate_keys), missing_ids = sum(missing_ids), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = st_measure_id) |>
  transmute(Measure = st_measure_id, Datasets = datasets, Rows = fmt(rows), `Participant-waves` = fmt(participants), `Duplicate keys` = fmt(duplicate_keys), `Rows with no ID` = fmt(missing_ids)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrr")
```

## Categorical variables against the schema

Advisory until `allowed_values` is maintained.

```{r}
#| label: allowed
violations |>
  filter(check == "outside_allowed_values") |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), cells = sum(n), .by = c(variable_name, detail)) |>
  arrange(desc(cells)) |>
  head(60) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, Level = detail, Datasets = datasets, Cells = fmt(cells)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrr", caption = "The 60 unlisted levels with most cells.")
```

## Continuous outcomes across datasets

One panel per variable with data in two or more datasets: each dataset's 5th to 95th percentile, quartiles and median.
Instruments differ between datasets on generic rows, so different locations are expected there; on instrument-specific rows they are not.

```{r}
#| label: outcome-panels
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 12
outcome_domains <- c("academic", "behaviour", "cognition", "mental_health", "wellbeing", "health", "family", "demographics")
numeric_vars <- schema |>
  filter(domain %in% outcome_domains, data_type == "double") |>
  select(variable_name, domain)
with_data <- numeric_summary |>
  filter(st_measure_id == "primary") |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = variable_name) |>
  filter(datasets >= 2) |>
  inner_join(numeric_vars, by = "variable_name")
for (domain_name in outcome_domains) {
  vars <- sort(with_data$variable_name[with_data$domain == domain_name])
  if (length(vars) == 0) next
  cat("\n\n### ", domain_name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (chunk in split(vars, ceiling(seq_along(vars) / 12))) {
    print(quantile_plot(chunk, ncol = 4))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```

## Every numeric variable, per dataset

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Table: n, mean, SD, median, MAD, minimum and maximum

```{r}
#| label: numeric-table
numeric_summary |>
  filter(st_measure_id == "primary") |>
  summarise(
    mean = weighted.mean(mean, n),
    sd = sqrt(weighted.mean(sd^2, n, na.rm = TRUE)),
    median = weighted.mean(median, n),
    mad = weighted.mean(mad, n),
    min = min(min),
    max = max(max),
    waves = n(),
    n = sum(n),
    .by = c(variable_name, dataset_id)
  ) |>
  arrange(variable_name, as.numeric(dataset_id)) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, Dataset = dataset_id, N = fmt(n), Waves = waves, Mean = signif(mean, 4), SD = signif(sd, 4), Median = signif(median, 4), MAD = signif(mad, 4), Min = signif(min, 4), Max = signif(max, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrrrrr")
```

Mean, median and MAD are averages of a dataset's waves, weighted by rows, and SD is the pooled within-wave SD.
:::

## Categorical levels against the schema

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Table: every level of every categorical variable

```{r}
#| label: level-table
level_summary |>
  filter(st_measure_id == "primary", level != "(many values)") |>
  left_join(schema[c("variable_name", "allowed_values")], by = "variable_name") |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = c(variable_name, level, allowed_values)) |>
  mutate(
    listed = case_when(
      is.na(allowed_values) ~ "no list",
      mapply(\(l, a) l %in% strsplit(a, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]], level, allowed_values) ~ "yes",
      TRUE ~ "NO"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(allowed_values)) |>
  arrange(variable_name, desc(n)) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, Level = level, `In allowed values` = listed, Datasets = datasets, Observations = fmt(n)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllrr")
```
:::
